claims.claim_text: The UK Government's Sovereign AI Venture Fund and the British Business Bank have backed Fractile, a London- and Bristol-based AI chip startup, as part of a funding round worth over £500 million.
claims.excerpt: has secured backing from the UK Government’s Sovereign AI Venture Fund and the British Business Bank as part of a round worth over £500 million.

claims.claim_text: The funding round values Fractile at over £5 billion.
claims.excerpt: Today’s funding round values the company at over £5 billion.

claims.claim_text: The round is a Series C that also includes investors such as CapitalG, Lightspeed and Redpoint.
claims.excerpt: it is also being backed through this Series C round by investors including CapitalG, Lightspeed and Redpoint.

claims.claim_text: The government says Fractile is re-inventing AI hardware to be faster, more energy efficient and less costly, working across chips, software and machine learning research.
claims.excerpt: Fractile is re-inventing the hardware that AI runs on, so that it is faster, more energy efficient, and less costly.

claims.claim_text: The investment was announced on Wednesday 11 November 2026.
The government does not disclose how much Sovereign AI itself invested, saying specific investment figures are commercially sensitive.
claims.excerpt: Like most venture capital funds we do not comment on specific investment figures as they are commercially sensitive

claims.claim_text: Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said Fractile plans to expand its presence in Bristol.
claims.excerpt: With plans to expand their presence in Bristol, Fractile are helping to put our plans for reindustrialisation into action

claims.claim_text: AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said Britain needs to build more of the technology that powers AI.
claims.excerpt: If AI is going to serve the British people, strengthen our public services and create good jobs across the country, Britain needs to build more of the technology that powers it.

claims.claim_text: At the Budget, the Chancellor confirmed a further £140 million for Sovereign AI, including £60 million for fund investments and £80 million for its R&D Procurement Scheme.
claims.excerpt: the Chancellor confirmed a further £140 million backing for Sovereign AI, with an additional £60 million to support the Fund’s investments, plus £80 million for Sovereign AI’s R&D Procurement Scheme.

claims.claim_text: The government says the investment aims to strengthen sovereign capabilities and reduce reliance on overseas technology supply chains.
claims.excerpt: Backing British companies will strengthen sovereign capabilities, reduce reliance on overseas technology and support highly skilled jobs and industrial renewal across the country
